Responsibilities

Our team focuses on the R&D of algorithm for TikTok international advertising customer growth. We leverage deep learning and large language model technologies to build an algorithmic system for advertiser acquisition and retention, optimize the operational efficiency of the international commerce platform, and empower the business to achieve sustainable long-term revenue growth.

What You'll Do
- Build the core "brain" of an AI agent for the advertising sales domain and track cutting-edge technologies. Explore mainstream Agent frameworks, continuously monitor the latest advancements in the AI Agent field, and introduce and validate the feasibility of new technologies—with a focus on enhancing automated task planning and scheduling, tool invocation, multimodal interaction, and deep research capabilities. Establish an Agent evaluation mechanism for Harness-driven iteration.
- Develop a Skills toolset for advertising sales and customer acquisition scenarios, building and optimizing a suite of high-performance, reusable Skills.
- Explore Agent automation and self-evolution, enabling the Agent to learn from real-world interaction data and continuously improve its decision-making and execution capabilities.
- Build stable and reliable Agent infrastructure, including performance and stability optimization of the Agent system.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
- Master's degree or higher in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, or related fields.
- Familiarity with at least one mainstream Agent framework (e.g., LangGraph, OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code, etc.) with hands-on experience.
- Deep understanding of the core principles of Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI Agents. Familiarity with mainstream Agent architectures (e.g., ReAct/PlanAct), Multi-Agent systems, and concepts such as Context Engineering and Memory.
- Solid AI/ML background with in-depth knowledge of post-training techniques such as SFT and RLHF. Practical experience in fine-tuning model capabilities for specific tasks is preferred.
- Excellent coding skills with strong fundamentals in data structures and algorithms. Proficiency in C/C++ or Python.
- Strong teamwork, collaboration, and communication skills.

TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo.​

Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.​
​
Diversity & Inclusion​
TikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.​

jobs.title: AI Engineer 5
jobs.description:
At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.

Team Description:

The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.

What You’ll Do:

Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, PyTorch, and more.
Invent and introduce state-of-the-art foundation model optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systems.
Contribute to the technical vision and the long term roadmap of foundational AI systems at Capital One.
Design, implement and optimize multi-model orchestration pipelines - integrating LLMs, vector search, and domain-specific models into unified systems
Establish and lead cost-performance governance reviews across AI systems, tracking GPU utilization, model throughput, and inference cost efficiency
Lead team design councils or design review boards to ensure technical consistency and compliance with AI engineering standards
Mentor Principal and Manager-level AI engineers, fostering cross-domain learning and elevating organizational technical maturity

The Ideal Candidate:

You love to build systems, take pride in the quality of your work, and also share our passion to do the right thing. You want to work on problems that will help change banking for good
Passion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
You adapt quickly and thrive on bringing clarity to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and digging deep to uncover the root of problems and can articulate your findings concisely with clarity. You have the courage to share new ideas even when they are unproven
You are deeply Technical. You possess a strong foundation in engineering and mathematics, and your expertise in hardware, software, and AI enables you to see and exploit optimization opportunities that others miss
You are a resilient trailblazer who can forge new paths to achieve business goals when the route is unknown

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 6 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies, or a Master's degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 4 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies
At least 6 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, CUDA, or Java

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience leading development AI systems with tradeoff decisions around cost, latency, throughput and accuracy
7+ years of experience deploying scalable and responsible AI solutions on cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or equivalent private cloud)
Experience designing, developing, delivering, and supporting complex AI systems
Experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies (e.g. LLM Inference, Similarity Search and VectorDBs, Guardrails, Memory) using Python, C++, C#, Java, CUDA, or Golang
Experience developing and applying state-of-the-art techniques for optimizing training and inference software to improve hardware utilization, latency, throughput, and cost
Experience in building agentic AI systems and agentic workflows
Passion for staying abreast of the latest AI research and AI systems, and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex AI concepts to peers
Experience architecting and integrating heterogeneous AI systems - including rule-based, retrieval-augmented, and generative components - into unified production pipelines
Experience defining and enforcing standards for ethical AI deployment, including explainability, fairness, and human-in-the-loop review processes
Demonstrated ability to balance model performance and operational cost through dynamic inference strategies and model compression
Experience right-sizing models, instance counts, and hardware types given requirements (e.g., context length, token inputs, token outputs)

About Accrete

Accrete builds Knowledge Engine products that combine organizational context, human expertise, and specialized agents for consequential work across enterprises and national security.
Accrete is a dynamic and innovative company focused on transforming the future of artificial intelligence. We specialize in creating advanced AI solutions that turn complex data into actionable insights, driving real-world impact for businesses and government organizations. Our team thrives on creativity and collaboration, working together to push the boundaries of AI technology. At the core of our offerings are AI agents-autonomous systems that analyze multimodal data, generate insights, and make intelligent recommendations. These agents help businesses streamline operations, improve decision-making, and empower government entities to enhance security, intelligence, and operational efficiency.

The Role

The forward deployed engineer sits at the intersection of data strategy and operational delivery of our AI products. Customers often have a strong instinct that their data can help them protect personnel, support campaigns, be more efficient, or deliver aid more safely, but without a specialist who can get them there. FDEs turn that instinct into working capability, and they keep the effort organized, unblocked, and on track while it happens.
You will join a small, collaborative team of engineers, product managers, and fellow FDEs to put software to work on difficult, high-stakes problems, with a focus on US Government engagements. Your job is to pull scattered inputs into a single, coherent view: which problem matters most, what the data is actually saying, what the product must do, what motivates the people using it, and where real impact can be achieved. You will also own the operational health of your projects, tracking progress, resolving obstacles early, and making sure delivery lands on time, within budget, and to a high standard.
If you believe in the power of data and technology to solve hard problems, and you are equally comfortable digging into the details and bringing structure to ambiguity, we would like to talk with you.

Work on site with customer analysts and operators to learn the key questions they must answer and the friction points that slow them down.
Locate and evaluate the datasets that matter most, then partner with engineers to bring them into reliable, scalable pipelines.
Design tailored workflows with customers for new groups of users.
Run training and enablement sessions so the product fits real needs and is adopted broadly enough to make a measurable difference to customer operations.
Share findings and recommendations with audiences from frontline analysts to senior executives.
Act as a first responder when problems surface, diagnosing issues and putting creative, practical fixes in place.
Find and clear bottlenecks, blockers, and friction so teammates can concentrate on the work they do best.
Build processes and tools that make better use of people, time, and resources.
Work with Accrete colleagues to identify process gaps, scope new initiatives, and deliver results on schedule, on budget, and at a high quality bar.
Collaborate with engineering and design teams to carry lessons from the field back into Accrete's broader product offerings.
Prepare and present demos for current and prospective customers.
Evaluate opportunities in new industries and geographies as Accrete's footprint grows.
Draw on the team's shared expertise, build new skills where gaps exist, and act on feedback to keep growing.

What We Value

Comfort with open-ended problems in unstructured, fast-moving environments without over-the-shoulder support.
Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and the instinct to spot inefficiencies and fix them quickly.
Clear, confident communication, including the ability to explain technical ideas to non-technical audiences.
Meticulous attention to detail, including accurate records and consistent tracking of project metrics.
Adaptability, self-awareness, and a willingness to learn, teach, lead, and follow as the situation requires.
Experience with programming, scripting, or statistical tools such as Python, R, Matlab, or SQL is a plus.

What We Require

A current US security clearance at the top secret level or above.

FDEs work in a high-accountability, high-expectation culture where the goal is always the best possible solution. Giving, receiving, and acting on feedback is essential, and so is supporting teammates who care as much about each other as they do about Accrete's mission.

About the Role

We are looking for a pragmatic, hands-on Data Scientist to build and own the quantitative foundation for our clinical care delivery, patient treatment plan refinement, and retention engines.

In our specialty care model, clinical health outcomes and business growth are directly linked: matching patients to their preferred, personalized treatment path leads to higher clinical efficacy, better satisfaction, and long-term retention. In this role, you won't just work with clean tabular data; you will bridge the gap between structured clinical metrics (lab values, symptom severity scores, dosage trajectories) and unstructured patient communications (visit transcripts, ambient scribe outputs, and intake survey dialogue).

You will sit at the intersection of Data Science, Clinical Operations, and Product, serving as a core builder who transforms messy, multi-modal patient data into actionable clinical decision support and personalized care pathways.

What You’ll Do

Data Foundation & Pipeline Development

Clean & Transform Multi-Modal Clinical Data:
Build reliable, well-structured modeling tables and feature stores by parsing, cleaning, and joining raw datasets including lab results, symptom severity surveys, medication history, and raw visit transcripts.
Establish Unstructured Data Workflows:
Design robust data processing pipelines to convert unstructured clinical notes, orders and visit transcripts into structured, queryable relational tables.

Transcript Mining & Feature Extraction

Extract Patient Intent & Preference:
Build lightweight NLP and LLM-based pipelines (using entity extraction, sentiment analysis, and topic modeling) to convert ambient visit transcripts into structured features. And provide insights into patient preferences in treatment pathway, communication, and modality, etc.
Identify Friction Points:
Process qualitative dialogue to automatically detect unaddressed obstacles or early side-effect reports before they lead to treatment discontinuation.

Lookalike Cohorts & Patient Treatment Planning

Lookalike Clustering Engine:
Develop unsupervised segmentation models to cluster patients into "lookalike" cohorts based on baseline lab values, symptom profiles, and transcript-derived preferences.
Outcome & Trajectory Forecasting:
Build predictive models that estimate symptom reduction, time-to-relief, and potential side-effect risks across alternative treatment branches (e.g., immediate HRT vs. conservative step-therapy).

Causal Inference & Retention Analytics

Quasi-Experimentation on Care Protocols:
Apply observational study methods (Propensity Score Matching, Difference-in-Differences, Survival Analysis) to evaluate non-randomized care pathways and quantify counterfactual patient outcomes.
Drop-Off & Retention Optimization:
Identify critical clinical touchpoints and dosage adjustment milestones that drive long-term program adherence, connecting clinical milestone achievement directly to patient retention and LTV.

Research & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Evidence Generation:
Partner with the clinical research team to provide analytical support for peer-reviewed medical publications, white papers, and payer studies.
Clinical Operations Alignment:
Translate analytical findings, treatment protocol insights, and patient drop-off trends into actionable workflow improvements for clinical operations and care teams.

What You Bring

Technical Skills

Programming & Querying:
Advanced proficiency in SQL for data manipulation alongside strong Python skills for predictive modeling and data transformation.
Machine Learning & Modeling:
Practical experience applying clustering (segmentation), regression/classification, and survival analysis (e.g., scikit-learn, statsmodels, lifelines).
NLP & Modern LLM Workflows:
Hands-on experience with NLP techniques and LLM frameworks (e.g., transformers, Claude API, etc.) to parse, extract, and classify unstructured text data.
Causal Inference Fundamentals:
Solid working knowledge of quasi-experimental design, propensity score matching, and counterfactual reasoning on observational datasets.

Analytical Capabilities

Healthcare Data Intuition:
Comfort working with messy, semi-structured, or missing healthcare datasets (lab results, Patient-Reported Outcome Measures/PROMs, EHR notes).
Pragmatic "0-to-1" Builder Mindset:
You enjoy doing the foundational data architecture work—cleaning JSON outputs, structuring features, and validating baseline models—before reaching for complex algorithms.
Cross-Functional Communication:
Ability to translate technical modeling outcomes into clear, intuitive insights for Clinical Operations and Product partners.

Experience

2 to 4 years of hands-on data science or analytics experience delivering high-impact solutions.
Experience working with healthcare, telehealth, digital health datasets.
Demonstrated track record of parsing unstructured text/transcript data into structured modeling pipelines.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Biomedical Data Science, Health Informatics, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative field.

Lumafield was founded in 2019 to upgrade manufacturing.

We are engineers with deep experience across the product development cycle, from initial ideas to shipping hardware, across industries and specializations, who became frustrated by the cost and complexity of modern manufacturing. So we decided to upgrade it.

Engineers make million-dollar decisions every day, and they need tools that give them the greatest possible insight into their products. We rebuilt the whole system, from X-ray capture, to computer vision analysis, to web-based collaboration, to the entire business model, making the most advanced manufacturing tech more accessible to every industry. new_jobs.title: Agentic AI Engineer, Life Science
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Algen is an AI-native precision medicine company harnessing the power of CRISPR and functional genomics to transform drug discovery and development. A spin-out from the laboratory of Nobel Laureate Professor Jennifer Doudna, Algen was founded at the forefront of gene-editing innovation. We combine cutting-edge CRISPR technologies with advanced AI approaches to systematically modulate disease biology at scale and accelerate the path to effective treatments. Join us in redefining what's possible in AI-powered drug discovery.

Job Description

As an Agentic AI Engineer (Life Science), you’ll build the software that lets an AI agent plan a scientific analysis, choose tools and recover when a step fails. You’ll work with biologists and chemists to define what a successful analysis looks like, then use those criteria to decide which changes to ship. The work includes bringing the latest advances and original ideas into production. The ideal candidate combines strong engineering execution with a quantitative mindset and an interest in AI agents for scientific discovery.

Responsibilities

Advance the agent harness by bringing the latest research and open-source developments into production and experimenting with new approaches to multi-agent coordination, model routing, memory, planning, and tool use.
Work with biologists and chemists to turn real research questions into test cases. Agree on what evidence an answer needs and record the steps a scientist would need to check it.
Compare changes against a baseline on representative tasks. Measure scientific correctness, completion rate, latency and cost before deciding whether to release a change.
Make long-running analyses resilient. Run code in a sandbox with scoped tool access, save progress and let interrupted jobs resume without repeating completed work.
Trace production failures from the agent’s decision through its tool calls and outputs. Reproduce the failure, fix it and add a test that catches it on the next release.

Qualifications

MUST HAVE:
2+ years of industry experience building production software, with hands-on ownership of a backend service, infrastructure component or full-stack feature.
MUST HAVE:
Familiarity with LLM APIs, tool calling, agent runtimes, or workflow orchestration.
MUST HAVE:
Research or production experience building an LLM-powered agent that calls tools or coordinates a workflow. You can explain a design choice you made and how you tested it.
MUST HAVE:
Experience using data to judge a system change. You can design a repeatable comparison, investigate inconsistent results and explain the tradeoffs to colleagues.
Ability to take an engineering problem from design through testing, deployment and debugging, and to write code that teammates can maintain.
Ability to move between research questions, data analysis, system design, and production implementation.
Experience or strong interest in AI for science, scientific agents, computational research, or automated scientific discovery.
Experience building modern web applications (e.g. React, TypeScript, FastAPI, or similar frameworks).
Ability to move fast, own features end-to-end, and operate with high autonomy.
High standards for code quality, maintainability, and engineering excellence. .

Preferred

Experience designing benchmarks for LLMs, reviewing outputs with domain experts or replaying past runs to test for regressions.
Experience with durable workflows, task queues, sandboxed code execution or tools for inspecting distributed jobs.
Experience with LLM post-training, including fine-tuning models for tool use or scientific tasks
Experience developing agent systems for scientific discovery, particularly self-evolving agents.
Research or graduate-level experience in machine learning, computational biology or another quantitative field.

new_jobs.description:
Description

A Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to independently design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDE IIs write production-grade software and own delivery of complete AI workstreams end-to-end — from requirements gathering through production deployment — combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes.

FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. They design cohesive implementations for well-understood problems, making design trade-offs with appropriate guidance. They take on projects where the business problem is understood but implementations are not fully fleshed out, balancing constraints and limiting short-term workarounds. They coach others on producing high-quality code and train new team members.

Key job responsibilities

Embed within customer engineering teams. Work with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand the business and customer value of the systems you build. Understand the customer's business processes, technical architecture, and operational constraints. Translate customer requirements into technical designs for AI-enabled production systems within your workstream. Requires 30 – 50% travel.
Build production AI applications. Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.
Own production for your workstream. Be a significant contributor to the full software development lifecycle including scoping, design, code, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Troubleshoot production incidents across AI models, distributed systems, and application services. Ensure root causes of operational issues are identified and resolved. Implement monitoring, evaluations, guardrails, and CI/CD that keep AI systems healthy. Don't settle for the status quo — routinely identify and execute on opportunities to improve operations.
Mentor and uplift. Actively mentors and trains new team members on how systems are constructed, operated, and fit into the bigger picture. Coach others on producing high-quality code through mechanisms such as code review. Be active in the code review process, providing meaningful feedback to others.

new_jobs.description:
Department: Strategic Engineering | Reports to: James Trebesch, Head of Strategic Engineering | Employment: Full-Time
Office Location: Palo Alto, California
Proposed Annual Base Salary: $190,000–$250,000
Plus significant equity and comprehensive benefits.
About the Role
We are seeking a Senior AI Compute & Networking Engineer to lead the development and optimization of standardized GPU compute and networking infrastructure for AI data centers. This role owns compute and networking reference architectures, evaluates NVIDIA and other GPU platform requirements, and establishes repeatable cluster, network, and rack configurations that connect directly to physical facility requirements. The engineer will lead technical work with OEMs, vendors, integrators, and external consultants while collaborating with software teams to translate customer requirements into configuration logic, equipment selection, bills of materials, and procurement workflows. This is a systems engineering and infrastructure product role, not routine network administration.
Key Responsibilities
Compute & Networking Architecture
• Own Remanie’s AI compute and networking reference architectures, standards, and approved configurations.
• Develop reusable GPU cluster options based on workload, GPU platform, cluster size, networking, and expansion requirements.
• Evaluate NVIDIA DGX, HGX, DGX SuperPOD, rack-scale GPU systems, and emerging reference designs.
• Define training, inference, storage, and management network topologies, including bandwidth, latency, cabling, and connectivity.
• Standardize rack configurations, networking equipment, physical layouts, and interfaces with power and cooling.
• Translate compute decisions into electrical demand, heat rejection, liquid-cooling requirements, space planning, and facility interfaces.
• Optimize for performance, hardware utilization, capital cost, technical compatibility, availability, and deployment speed.
Engineering Software & Procurement Development
• Translate customer GPU, workload, network, and expansion requirements into structured software inputs and configuration logic.
• Define hardware compatibility constraints, architecture-selection criteria, qualified equipment options, and cross-system dependencies.
• Support automated preliminary compute/network architecture, equipment schedules, bills of materials, and procurement packages.
• Incorporate OEM lead times, supplier availability, costs, and substitutions into equipment selection rules.
• Validate software-generated configurations against platform requirements and deployment constraints.
• Help build the requirements-to-configured-and-purchasable-data-center workflow; refresh software logic as technologies evolve.
External Engineering, OEM & Vendor Leadership
• Direct equipment manufacturers, systems integrators, and external technical partners responsible for detailed design and implementation.
• Establish reference specifications, work scopes, technical integration criteria, and review requirements.
• Challenge OEM proposals, cluster configurations, network designs, and vendor assumptions.
• Identify and maintain approved equipment configurations and qualified alternative suppliers.
• Coordinate with facility engineering firms so compute requirements appear correctly in detailed electrical, mechanical, and civil designs.
• Standardize equipment installation, integration, testing, commissioning, and deployment requirements.
Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration
• Work with electrical, mechanical, and civil disciplines to define integrated infrastructure products.
• Support customer technical discovery and evaluate implications of new GPU and networking generations.
• Incorporate deployment, commissioning, and operational feedback into revised reference systems.
Required Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
• Significant AI compute, high-performance computing, hyperscale data-center, or large-scale network experience.
• Demonstrated design or architecture experience with GPU clusters, high-performance networks, or large compute environments.
• Strong understanding of InfiniBand, high-speed Ethernet, network topology, and AI cluster connectivity.
• Familiarity with NVIDIA GPU platforms and associated infrastructure requirements.
• Experience evaluating technical architectures, OEM equipment, integration constraints, and system-level tradeoffs.
• Ability to lead external technical partners and understand rack-level power, thermal, and facility interfaces.
Preferred Qualifications
• Direct NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, HGX, or large-scale AI cluster deployment experience.
• NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Quantum InfiniBand, or comparable high-performance networking systems.
• Standardized compute/network reference design development.
• Hyperscaler, GPU manufacturer, OEM, systems integrator, or AI infrastructure developer experience.
• High-density, liquid-cooled AI compute deployments.
• Infrastructure configurators, automated architecture tools, structured product data, and BOM generation.
• Compute hardware supply chain, supplier qualification, procurement, and deployment/commissioning workflows.
What Success Looks Like
• Validated, reusable compute and networking configurations for customer requirements.
• Software-generated compute/network equipment packages and clear power, cooling, and site interfaces.
• Less custom design and integration work with faster, more reliable procurement and delivery.
Why Join Remanie
This foundational role reports directly to the Head of Strategic Engineering and shapes the compute backbone of Remanie’s requirements-to-purchase infrastructure platform. Software coding is not required; translating compute expertise into structured product logic is essential. As the platform evolves, the same engineering and procurement capabilities may also support adjacent markets such as robotics and industrial automation.

AI Engineer [Senior Associate / AVP]

Founded in 1992, Cerberus is a global leader in alternative investing with approximately $71 billion in assets across complementary credit, private equity, and real estate strategies. We invest across the capital structure where our integrated investment platforms and proprietary operating capabilities create an edge to improve performance and drive long-term value. Our tenured teams have experience working collaboratively across asset classes, sectors, and geographies to seek strong risk-adjusted returns for our investors. For more information about our people and platforms, visit us at www.cerberus.com.

About Us

We are a new, but growing team of AI specialists - software engineers focused on AI development, and technology strategists - working to transform how an alternative investment firm with $65B in assets under management leverages technology and data. Our remit is broad, spanning investment operations, portfolio companies, and internal systems, giving the team the opportunity to shape the way the firm approaches analytics, automation, and decision-making.

We operate with the creativity and agility of a small team, tackling diverse, high-impact challenges across the firm. While we are embedded within a global investment platform, we maintain a collaborative, innovative culture where our AI talent can experiment, learn, and have real influence on business outcomes.

About the job

As a software engineer on the AI team at Cerberus, you’ll build internal applications that help our investment teams and portfolio companies use AI, data and automation in real workflows. This role is about taking high-value business problems from rough idea to working product, including full-stack apps, workflow automations, and AI-enabled tools.

You’ll design, implement and operate production-grade applications across the stack: Python services, APIs, React and TypeScript frontends, relational databases, SQL, orchestration layers, integrations with enterprise data sources, and LLM-powered agentic workflows.

We’re looking for engineers who care about impact: people who can prototype quickly, make pragmatic technical trade-offs, work closely with business and product stakeholders, and turn emerging AI capabilities into reliable products that users actually adopt.

Responsibilities

Build internal AI-enabled applications: Design and deliver full-stack applications that solve real business problems across investment workflows, portfolio operations, analytics, data management and process automation.
Build on top of enterprise data and workflows: Develop applications and workflows that sit on top of structured business data, internal systems and third-party tools, whether that is Microsoft Fabric, Rayfin, relational databases, APIs or other environments.
Develop across the stack: Build backend services and APIs in Python using FastAPI or similar frameworks, and create user-facing workflows and interfaces using React and TypeScript.
Implement AI agents in code: Build and integrate AI agents for use cases such as analytics, data management, application building and business process automation, using LLM provider APIs such as OpenAI or Anthropic.
Turn prototypes into products: Take rough ideas, user pain points and proof-of-concepts through rapid iteration, user testing and, where appropriate, production deployment.
Orchestrate reliable workflows: Use orchestration patterns and tools such as Temporal or similar systems to make multi-step workflows reliable, observable and maintainable.
Engineer for adoption and maintainability: Partner with investment teams, portfolio companies, product managers and business stakeholders to make applications useful, usable, secure and supportable.
Make pragmatic trade-offs: Balance speed, quality, security, cost and maintainability in a fast-moving environment where the goal is to create measurable business value.

Sample Projects You’ll Work On

Data-driven business applications: Build applications that sit on top of structured data assets and workflow tools, enabling users to explore, update, enrich or act on information through intuitive workflows rather than static dashboards alone.
AI agents for analytics and data management: Develop agents that can query data, perform analysis, generate structured outputs, validate information, and support repeatable business processes with appropriate controls and human review.
Workflow automation and internal tools: Build full-stack applications that connect internal systems, proprietary data sources, third-party APIs and AI services into structured workflows for investment, operations or portfolio company teams.
Prototype-to-production applications: Work with business and product stakeholders to turn a rough idea into a POC, test it with users, refine the workflow, and harden the solution where there is clear business value.

Your Experience

We’re a small, high-impact and entrepreneurial team with a broad remit. We’re looking for an Associate or Senior Associate-level software engineer with strong full-stack engineering fundamentals who is excited to build internal applications, AI-enabled products and data-driven tools. We don’t expect every candidate to check every box, but strong candidates will combine hands-on software engineering ability with sound product judgement and strong communication skills.
Strong software engineering foundation:
Degree in a STEM field or equivalent experience, with a track record of building reliable applications, backend services, internal tools, APIs or production systems.
Python expertise:
Skilled in writing production-grade Python, including clean APIs, type hints, testing, packaging and maintainable service design.
Backend development:
Experience building backend services and APIs using FastAPI or similar frameworks, with an ability to reason about reliability, maintainability, observability and system design.
Frontend development:
Experience building modern frontends using React and TypeScript, with an ability to create practical, usable interfaces for business users.
Databases and SQL:
Strong understanding of relational databases, data modelling and SQL, with the ability to write efficient, maintainable queries and work with structured business data.
Data applications:
Experience building applications, workflows or analytics products on top of enterprise data platforms, relational databases, APIs or business systems. Familiarity with tools such as Microsoft Fabric, Databricks or Rayfin is helpful but not required.
System architecture:
Experience working with distributed systems, monolithic systems, or both, and the judgement to choose the right architecture for the problem rather than over-engineering by default.
Workflow orchestration:
Exposure to Temporal or similar orchestrators is a plus, especially for multi-step, long-running or failure-prone workflows.
AI/ML tooling and agent development:
Experience building or implementing AI agents in code for use cases such as analytics, data management, application building or business process automation.
LLM provider APIs:
Experience interacting with LLM provider APIs such as OpenAI, Anthropic or similar services, including tool use, structured outputs, evaluation and monitoring considerations.
Agent frameworks and observability:
Familiarity with tools such as LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith or Langfuse is helpful but optional. We care more about sound engineering judgement than any single framework.
Vector databases and retrieval:
Experience with vector databases, embeddings or retrieval-augmented generation is useful but not required.
AI coding tools:
Familiarity with AI coding tools such as Claude, Cursor, Codex or similar tools, and the judgement to use them effectively while maintaining high engineering standards.
Engineering practices:
Strong habits around Git, testing, code reviews, CI/CD, documentation, monitoring and operational ownership. Experience with tools such as Sentry or Grafana is a plus.
Product and delivery judgement:
The technical skills to build across the full stack, combined with the judgement to know which problems are worth solving, when to prototype, when to harden, and when to stop.
Pragmatic execution:
Ability to take ambiguity, shape it into a concrete technical plan, build quickly, learn from users and make pragmatic trade-offs.
Communication and stakeholder management:
Strong communication, stakeholder management and business interaction skills, with the ability to work effectively with business users, product managers and technical colleagues.

For More Advanced or Senior Candidates

More senior candidates may bring a combination of the above skills together with experience designing AI systems or leading small AI-native engineering efforts. Additional strengths may include:
Designing AI platforms, application architectures or agentic systems.
Leading small engineering teams or technical workstreams.
Aligning engineering decisions with product priorities and business value.
Mentoring other engineers and improving team engineering practices.
Advanced prioritisation and delivery judgement in ambiguous environments.
Experience with AI governance, assurance, evaluation, security, permissions or agent sandboxes.
Strong understanding of software development best practices, especially in the age of AI-assisted engineering.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
ABOUT THE POSITION

Groundswell builds community power - cutting electricity bills for the neighbors who need savings most through community solar, resilience hubs, and home energy efficiency and repair. Gratava is the AI-enabled data platform underneath that work: a neutral coordination layer where a household proves eligibility once and that verified record unlocks every program they qualify for.

Forward deployed means living with our users, customers, and partners. The Forward Deployed Engineer will sit with utility staff, program administrators, caseworkers and households to find what blocks or limits adoption and success - then build the prototypes that prove the solution works, validate it with the customer, and hand it off to production engineering. Customer contact and building are one job here.

Reporting to the SVP, Data Platform, the Forward Deployed Engineer is a peer to the Tech Lead with distinct ownership: the Forward Deployed Engineer proves what should be built, and the Tech Lead is responsible for what ships in production. You will write production-quality code, and what you build is judged by whether it proves the answer rather than by whether it ships - deployment into production, and the policies and controls that go with it, stay with the Tech Lead.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Field discovery
. Work directly with our internal teams and with utilities, program administrators, agencies and households to understand where systems, policies, and data break down in practice. You will investigate hard problems such as premise resolution, income verification, eligibility determination, program matching, and other rules that have not yet been defined.
• Build the proof.
Turn ambiguous problems into working software. Build new core functionality at the prototype level - the matching engine, the rules-as-logic layer, the AI agent layer - connected to real data sources and run against real records. Be responsible for both demonstrating an idea and building enough of it to prove whether it works and adds value. Prototype here means scope, not craft - you write code good enough to run in production, even though production deployment is determined by the Tech Lead.
• Program rules into working logic
. Translate complex heterogeneous program
requirements into reliable, testable logic such as income thresholds, categorical
eligibility, funding stack sequencing, pre-weatherization gating and other program
specific conditions in ways that are explainable, auditable, and resilient.
• Validate with the customer.
Responsible for building prototypes and testing with
the people who will use them. Before production engineering begins, establish
three things: the data sources work as expected; the logic produces the correct
outcomes, and the interface is simple enough for customers to understand and
use.
• Create a clean path to production
. Deliver a working proof, the data connections,
technical decisions behind it, and a clear specification that distinguishes what is
essential from what is not. Give production engineering enough clarity to complete
the work without having to discover the problem.
• Scope the roadmap
. Turn technical discovery into actionable products and
engineering decisions. Provide fast, reliable feasibility assessments and effort
estimates that leadership and engineering can use to make and commit to
roadmap decisions.
• Continual Development and Growth
. Share what you know and learn with the
broader engineering team. Partner closely with the Tech Lead to transfer agentic
tooling practice and document knowledge that compounds across the team.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

As a member of the Groundswell team, the Forward Deployed Engineer is expected to
participate in the overall execution of Groundswell programs, including support for
program launches, partner engagements, and organization-wide initiatives as needs
arise.

OTHER DUTIES

This position description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of
activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required. Duties, obligations, and activities
may change at any time with or without notice.

COMPETENCIES OR SPECIALIZED KNOWLEDGE

• Writes production-ready code - able to work to production standards, and able to
judge when a proof is good enough to stop.
• Comfortable in the field with customers - builds fast, validates directly, and hands
off cleanly.
• Judgment about scope - knows what not to build while a customer is pushing, and
can defend it to a non-technical stakeholder.
• Comfort in regulated environments: consent, audit logging, role-based access, and
data governance.
• Able to work independently in an early-stage environment with limited scaffolding
and shifting priorities.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY

This position has no supervisory responsibility.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is based in Washington, D.C. and is expected to work in-office four days per
month in alignment with Groundswell’s hybrid/remote work plan.

POSITION TYPE AND EXPECTED HOURS

This is a full-time, 40-hour-a-week position. The days and hours of work are Monday
through Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, and core hours are from 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Occasional evening and weekend work may be required as job duties demand.

TRAVEL

Travel to program sites is expected roughly once a month, with heavier periods around
new deployments. Occasional visits to Groundswell office locations may also be required.

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field - or
equivalent practical experience. We weight demonstrated work over credentials.
• Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous, rules-heavy domain requirements
into working logic.
• Two to four years building with modern AI tools - Claude, OpenAI and equivalent
agentic development tools as normal practice.
• Salesforce and Slack experience.
• Preferred: energy, housing, healthcare, public benefits or other rules-based
program experience.

SUPERVISION

The Forward Deployed Engineer will report to Groundswell’s Senior Vice President of
Data Platform.

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position is within the range of $130,000 - $160,000 consistent
within Groundswell’s established pay band for this role. This is a full-time position, eligible
for Groundswell’s comprehensive employee benefits package.

BENEFITS

• Groundswell pays 100% of the monthly premium for health, dental, vision, and
long-term disability for full-time employees in accordance with Groundswell’s
policy. Groundswell also covers 50% of spouses and dependents covered under
the Groundswell healthcare, vision, and dental plan.
• Matching 401 (k) plan contribution by Groundswell up to 4% for employees who
choose to contribute to Groundswell’s 401 (k) plan, with immediate vesting.
• Monthly Development Days to focus on professional development opportunities.
• $45 per month to reimburse cellular phone use for business purposes.
• $75 per month to reimburse home internet access for business purposes.
• Fifteen (15) paid vacation days per year; eight (8) sick days; and two (2) personal
days. Vacation and sick leave accrue at the start of your employment, restart each
year on January 1, and increase with tenure. Personal days begin after six months
of employment.
• Groundswell also takes nine (9) paid federal holidays and a holiday break from
December 24th to January 1st (inclusive).
• Short-Term Disability Insurance, Long-Term Disability Insurance, and Voluntary
Life available.
• Pre-tax benefits such as Smart Benefits, Flexible spending accounts, and
Dependent care are also available.

For more information about the organization’s benefits and other personnel policies,
Groundswell will provide a new hire orientation within the first week of employment.

HOW TO APPLY

Submit a resume and cover letter to hiring@groundswell.org. Groundswell is an equal opportunity
employer deeply committed to the principles of equity, diversity and
inclusiveness.

new_jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is an early-stage AI company building a new kind of context and intelligence platform for product teams. Their technology brings together the information teams rely on: decisions, customer research, project pipelines, institutional knowledge, and other critical business context, making it accessible to both people and AI agents across the tools where work happens.

Our client is rethinking how products get built in an AI-native world.
As AI dramatically accelerates execution, the boundaries between product, design, and engineering are becoming less defined. Increasingly, the differentiators are judgment, creativity, customer understanding, and the ability to turn ambiguity into something useful.

That philosophy shapes both the product and the team. Rather than operating within narrow functional lanes, team members are expected to think across product, technology, design, and customer experience and take ownership from idea through execution.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Product Engineer / Product Builder to help enterprise customers successfully adopt both the platform and a new way of building products.
This is an unusual role at the intersection of product management, management consulting, customer strategy, change management, and hands-on AI development.

You’ll embed with enterprise customers — including large, complex organizations — to understand how their teams currently operate, identify what is slowing them down, integrate the platform into their workflows, and help them fundamentally improve how they build products.
Technology is only part of the challenge. Success also requires navigating organizational dynamics, earning trust, facilitating change, and helping teams adopt new behaviors that stick. As such, it will require heavy travel ( w/in North America and Internationally).

Think of this as a PM or management consultant who also loves to build.
You’ll work closely with the founding team, learn a proven methodology for improving product velocity, and take ownership of bringing that methodology to life inside customer organizations.

What You’ll Do

Embed with enterprise customers.
Partner closely with product managers, engineering leaders, technical founders, and senior stakeholders to understand how their organizations operate, where work gets stuck, and what is really preventing teams from moving faster.
Turn messy environments into effective systems.
Integrate the platform into each customer's existing decisions, research, knowledge, and work pipelines so teams — and the AI agents supporting them — can operate with better context and greater specificity.
Lead organizational change.
Help teams move away from long-established habits and adopt new ways of working. You'll need to understand resistance, build trust, create internal champions, and drive adoption without creating unnecessary disruption.
Teach and facilitate.
Lead workshops and working sessions that help customers understand not only how to use the technology, but why the underlying methodology works. You'll be comfortable answering hard questions and winning over skeptical audiences.
Build alongside customers.
This isn't a role where you'll simply make recommendations and hand them off. You'll prototype, configure, experiment, and demonstrate solutions yourself.
Bring the customer into the product roadmap.
Translate what you're seeing in the field into clear, actionable product insights. Your exposure to different organizations and use cases will directly influence how the platform evolves.
Drive measurable results.
Ultimately, your work should help customers build better products faster. You'll take ownership of each deployment and work toward demonstrable improvements in adoption, decision-making, and product velocity.

What We’re Looking For

You have strong product management fluency.
You understand product discovery, prioritization, customer research, product velocity, experimentation, and the realities of getting products shipped. More importantly, you've applied these concepts in real organizations.

Salvo Software is a global technology company specializing in custom software development and advanced engineering solutions. With distributed teams across the US, LATAM, and India, we partner with clients to build high-performance, scalable systems that solve complex technical challenges. Our culture values innovation, ownership, and engineering excellence. We're growing our AI department and are looking for a hands-on AI Developer to help build it.

Role Overview

We are looking for an AI Developer to join and strengthen our AI department. Your core work will be building and operating LLM-powered systems: serving open-source models with Ollama and llama.cpp, building RAG pipelines, and developing MCP integrations that connect large language models to real tools and data. Solid DevOps fundamentals - Docker, CI/CD, Azure - support this work, but AI engineering is the heart of the role.

You don't need to be a deep ML researcher. What matters is production-grade Python, strong fundamentals, and the aptitude to learn fast. You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams to take LLM-powered features from prototype to reliably deployed systems, with mentorship available as you ramp up in areas like RAG architecture, Kafka, and advanced MCP work.

Key Responsibilities

AI / LLM Engineering (core focus)

Serve and operate open-source LLMs using Ollama and llama.cpp, locally and in on-prem environments.
Build and maintain RAG pipelines: embeddings, vector databases, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality.
Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations connecting LLMs to internal tools and data sources.
Build backend services in Python that power ML inference and AI-driven product features.
Parse and process structured and semi-structured data (XML/XSD, Office document formats) as pipeline inputs.
Grow into model optimization over time: quantization (GGUF), GPU/CUDA tuning, and offline/air-gapped deployments.

DevOps & Infrastructure (supporting)

Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI services (Azure DevOps preferred; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI also used).
Deploy AI workloads to Microsoft Azure,AWS and containerize services with Docker.
Automate operational tasks with Python, Bash and/or PowerShell scripting.
Troubleshoot across the stack - dig into root causes rather than patching symptoms.
Support event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka (producers/consumers).

Requirements

3–5+ years engineering experience with production-level Python for building real services, LLM inference, RAG pipelines, and automated tooling.
Hands-on LLM & AI integration serving models via Ollama/llama.cpp, implementing vector retrieval/RAG, and developing MCP integrations (GPU/CUDA tuning & model quantization nice to have).
Cloud & Infrastructure expertise covering Azure/AWS deployments, Docker containerization, Linux/Windows admin, and CI/CD automation (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI), with Terraform, Kubernetes, Kafka, or systems languages (Go, Rust, C++) as a plus.
DevOps, Security & Operations awareness, including Git workflows, scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell), observability tools (Prometheus/Grafana), DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Zero Trust).
Strong problem-solving & communication with a root-cause troubleshooting mindset, self-directed learning, strong ownership, and seamless remote/distributed team collaboration.

Have a direct business impact on Live, Global E-Commerce, Local Services and many business domains.

Participate in the architecture, scale-testing, and maintenance of massive distributed computing foundations, GPU cluster configurations, and orchestration pipelines to achieve high hardware utilization and cluster efficiency under established SLI/SLO frameworks.

About OpenMined

OpenMined is a 501(c)(3) non-profit foundation that brings together leading minds in AI, security, and privacy technology to develop open-source solutions that transform how data can be accessed and shared. Founded in 2017, we've grown into a global community of over 18,000 members working to ensure that privacy protection and AI innovation reinforce each other rather than undermine one another. We are driven by a simple challenge: the most valuable data for solving humanity's greatest challenges remains locked away due to privacy concerns, and we can change that through technology rather than compromise.

About The Role

OpenMined is a nonprofit building open-source infrastructure for federated AI. Our AI Oversight team is the only team in the world working on external access to frontier AI labs. We build the privacy-preserving infrastructure that lets independent evaluators run evaluations on frontier AI models without exposing the models or anyone's private data.

As a Senior Software Engineer, reporting to the Technical Lead Manager, AI Oversight, you'll build core parts of this system and the products on top of it. You'll also work directly with organizations to deploy our software in their environments, so their data can be used while it stays private and under their control. Our software is moving from its first production deployment to several, with frontier labs and external evaluators, and we're adding senior engineers who can own big pieces of it.

This is a hands-on role for a strong general engineer: someone who writes excellent code, makes design decisions that hold up, and explains their work clearly.

This is a fully remote role for people based in the United States, working within one hour of US Eastern Time.

Responsibilities

Design, build and ship core infrastructure for privacy-preserving AI evaluation, mostly in Python
Build and strengthen our secure enclave (TEE) solutions
Extend PySyft, our open-source library, including workers and verified receipts
Deploy and support our software in partner environments (frontier labs, evaluators, governments), and make those deployments reliable
Help take the product from one production deployment to several, improving reliability, scale and user experience
Write clean, tested, readable code, and review your teammates' work
Turn ambiguous requirements into clear designs, and explain trade-offs to engineers and non-engineers
Use AI coding tools to move fast while keeping quality high

Requirements

Must-Haves

5+ years of professional engineering experience, with strong Python skills
Excellent hands-on coding: you write code every day, and it's clean, reliable, readable, and well-tested
Strong understanding of software architecture, systems design, and engineering trade-offs: your designs hold up without big rework
Strong communication skills, including explaining technical ideas, timelines, risks, and trade-offs clearly and concisely
Full-stack experience on at least one project (backend, data, frontend, deployment). It's fine if one area isn't your strongest.
Experience with CI/CD, debugging complex systems, and working with cloud infrastructure
Familiarity with security, scalability, and reliability considerations
Ability to quickly understand unfamiliar concepts and turn them into practical solutions
Collaborative, adaptable, and comfortable giving and receiving constructive feedback on a small, fully remote team

Preferred

Secure enclaves (TEEs), confidential computing, or other security work
Experience with distributed systems
Experience deploying software into other organizations' environments
Terraform, Kubernetes, and cloud platforms such as Google Cloud or AWS
Experience with AI safety, privacy-enhancing technologies, or language models
Contributions to open-source projects, especially repos you own or meaningful contributions to others
Experience building products for developers
Experience working in a startup environment
A lower-level language (Rust, Go, C++) for performance-critical work

Compensation

Salary Range: $125,000 - $220,000 per year.
Actual offers will be determined based on the candidate's skills, level of experience, and location.

Benefits

Mission-Driven Work: Be part of a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, focused on social impact rather than profit, offering the chance to make a meaningful difference in the world.
US employee benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance with company contributions; Retirement: 403(b) plan, the 401(k) equivalent for non-profits

new_jobs.title: Solution Architect
new_jobs.description:
Solution Architect – Level 1 (Java Full Stack, E-commerce & Auth0)

Experience:
10–14 Years
Location:
Columbus, Ohio, USA
Position Summary

We are seeking a Solution Architect – Level 1 with strong expertise in Java-based full-stack development, enterprise e-commerce platforms, microservices architecture, and Auth0-based Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM).
The ideal candidate will be responsible for defining and driving application architecture, designing secure and scalable digital commerce solutions, and establishing identity and access management patterns across customer-facing web and mobile applications.
This role requires a strong technical foundation in Java, Spring Boot, distributed systems, modern frontend frameworks, cloud-native technologies, and identity standards, along with the ability to translate business requirements into robust architectural solutions.
The architect will collaborate with enterprise architects, product owners, engineering teams, security stakeholders, and business partners to ensure that solutions meet functional, non-functional, security, performance, and scalability requirements.
Key Responsibilities

1. Solution Architecture & Technical Design

Define solution architecture for enterprise-grade e-commerce applications and digital commerce ecosystems.
Translate business requirements and functional specifications into architecture blueprints, solution designs, and technical implementation guidelines.
Design scalable, resilient, loosely coupled microservices and API-driven architectures using Java and Spring Boot.
Define application components, service boundaries, integration patterns, data flows, and technology choices.
Establish architectural standards, reusable design patterns, coding guidelines, and engineering best practices.
Prepare High-Level Design (HLD), Low-Level Design (LLD), architecture diagrams, sequence diagrams, and deployment views.
Evaluate architectural trade-offs involving scalability, performance, maintainability, security, cost, and time to market.

2. Auth0, CIAM & Security Architecture

Design and govern Auth0-based identity and access management solutions for customer-facing e-commerce platforms.
Define authentication and authorization architecture using OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), JWT, and SAML where applicable.
Architect Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), social login, enterprise federation, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
Define secure identity integration patterns for web applications, mobile applications, backend services, and third-party platforms.
Establish token validation, session management, API security, identity lifecycle, and access control standards.
Design secure customer identity journeys, including registration, login, account recovery, profile management, and identity federation.
Collaborate with security and compliance teams to address identity risks, application vulnerabilities, and security requirements.
Define secure integration patterns between Auth0, API gateways, microservices, and external identity providers.

3. E-commerce & Digital Commerce Architecture

Design end-to-end architecture for B2B and B2C e-commerce platforms.
Define integration strategies for product catalogs, pricing, promotions, carts, checkout, payments, orders, and customer profiles.
Architect secure integrations with payment gateways, customer data platforms, CRM systems, and third-party commerce services.
Evaluate and design headless commerce and API-first digital commerce solutions.
Define reusable integration components and reference architectures to accelerate onboarding of multiple e-commerce clients or projects.
Ensure architecture supports high transaction volumes, availability, extensibility, and seamless customer experiences.

4. API, Microservices & Integration Architecture

Define REST API standards, service contracts, versioning, error handling, and backward compatibility.
Design synchronous and asynchronous integration patterns, including event-driven architecture where appropriate.
Establish API security, throttling, resiliency, observability, and fault-tolerance standards.
Define integration patterns between frontend applications, backend services, identity platforms, and external systems.
Identify opportunities to reduce point-to-point integrations and improve platform reusability.

5. Cloud-Native Architecture & DevOps

Design cloud-ready and cloud-native application architectures on AWS and/or Azure.
Define containerization, deployment, scaling, and orchestration strategies using Docker and Kubernetes.
Collaborate with DevOps teams on CI/CD pipelines, release management, infrastructure automation, and environment strategy.
Establish observability standards covering logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, and production diagnostics.
Evaluate cloud service capabilities, resilience patterns, disaster recovery, availability, and operational cost optimization.

6. Data, Performance & Reliability

Define data architecture and persistence strategies using relational and NoSQL databases.
Establish data ownership, transaction boundaries, caching, consistency, and data access patterns.
Define non-functional requirements and performance benchmarks for critical customer journeys.
Guide performance engineering, capacity planning, load testing, and bottleneck analysis.
Design for fault tolerance, graceful degradation, high availability, and disaster recovery.

7. Architecture Governance & Technical Leadership

Lead architecture reviews, technical design reviews, and solution walkthroughs.
Validate implementation against approved architecture, security standards, and engineering guidelines.
Guide technical leads and development teams throughout design, development, testing, and production deployment.
Identify technical risks, dependencies, architectural gaps, and modernization opportunities.
Mentor engineers and promote reusable components, consistent implementation patterns, and continuous improvement.
Communicate architecture decisions and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Support estimation, solution feasibility assessments, technical proposals, and delivery planning.

Required Technical Skills

Architecture & Design

Solution architecture and application architecture
High-Level Design (HLD) and Low-Level Design (LLD)
Microservices and distributed systems
REST API and integration architecture
Design patterns, SOLID principles, and domain-driven design concepts
Event-driven architecture and enterprise integration patterns

Backend Technologies

Java 8/11/17 or later
Spring Boot and Spring Security
Hibernate/JPA
RESTful services and microservices

new_jobs.title: AI Engineer 5
new_jobs.description:
At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.

Team Description:

The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.

What You’ll Do:

Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, PyTorch, and more.
Invent and introduce state-of-the-art foundation model optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systems.
Contribute to the technical vision and the long term roadmap of foundational AI systems at Capital One.
Design, implement and optimize multi-model orchestration pipelines - integrating LLMs, vector search, and domain-specific models into unified systems
Establish and lead cost-performance governance reviews across AI systems, tracking GPU utilization, model throughput, and inference cost efficiency
Lead team design councils or design review boards to ensure technical consistency and compliance with AI engineering standards
Mentor Principal and Manager-level AI engineers, fostering cross-domain learning and elevating organizational technical maturity

The Ideal Candidate:

You love to build systems, take pride in the quality of your work, and also share our passion to do the right thing. You want to work on problems that will help change banking for good
Passion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
You adapt quickly and thrive on bringing clarity to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and digging deep to uncover the root of problems and can articulate your findings concisely with clarity. You have the courage to share new ideas even when they are unproven
You are deeply Technical. You possess a strong foundation in engineering and mathematics, and your expertise in hardware, software, and AI enables you to see and exploit optimization opportunities that others miss
You are a resilient trailblazer who can forge new paths to achieve business goals when the route is unknown

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 6 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies, or a Master's degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 4 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies
At least 6 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, CUDA, or Java

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience leading development AI systems with tradeoff decisions around cost, latency, throughput and accuracy
7+ years of experience deploying scalable and responsible AI solutions on cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or equivalent private cloud)
Experience designing, developing, delivering, and supporting complex AI systems
Experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies (e.g. LLM Inference, Similarity Search and VectorDBs, Guardrails, Memory) using Python, C++, C#, Java, CUDA, or Golang
Experience developing and applying state-of-the-art techniques for optimizing training and inference software to improve hardware utilization, latency, throughput, and cost
Experience in building agentic AI systems and agentic workflows
Passion for staying abreast of the latest AI research and AI systems, and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate complex AI concepts to peers
Experience architecting and integrating heterogeneous AI systems - including rule-based, retrieval-augmented, and generative components - into unified production pipelines
Experience defining and enforcing standards for ethical AI deployment, including explainability, fairness, and human-in-the-loop review processes
Demonstrated ability to balance model performance and operational cost through dynamic inference strategies and model compression
Experience right-sizing models, instance counts, and hardware types given requirements (e.g., context length, token inputs, token outputs)
